seeds.text: Your personality may be the mask your nervous system built to stay safe. Stripping it isn't the goal — knowing it is.
You don't need to master your body. You need to learn to listen — most of us were taught to override it instead.
Healing begins the moment you stop calling your wounds your personality.
You're not crazy. You're carrying something heavier than one lifetime — and no one taught you it could be put down.
Healing doesn't happen through understanding. It happens through the body finally moving the energy that froze.

slides.composition: A luminous, chrome-plated, abstract architectural vault, slightly ajar, with subtle iridescent light leaking from within, framed centrally with a low angle.

slides.text: The parts of you built to survive became who you thought you were.
slides.composition: Two chrome-plated, cel-shaded anime hands, one gently pulling back a holographic, shimmering veil from a shadowed, featureless face, revealing soft light.

slides.text: Your system learned behaviors to stay safe. You called that "me."
slides.composition: An ornate, tribal chrome circuitry pattern glowing with internal energy, overlaid onto a subtle starry nebula background, hinting at complex internal workings.

slides.text: Being "too much" or "not enough" was a brilliant adaptation. It kept you hidden, protected.
slides.composition: A solitary, shimmering chrome figure, back turned, observing a vast, painterly cosmic landscape filled with soft glowing orbs, conveying a sense of quiet watchfulness.

slides.text: Healing isn't stripping off the mask. It's noticing *when* you put it on.
slides.composition: A close-up, top-down view of a single liquid-chrome teardrop reflecting a tiny, focused beam of prismatic light against a textured, deep navy ground.

slides.text: You don't have to carry the silent echoes of old fear, felt in your bones.
slides.composition: A glitching, fragmented marble statue of a torso, with cracks revealing glowing, flowing liquid silver underneath, set against a dark, textured void.

slides.text: What if who you *really* are doesn't need protecting anymore?
slides.composition: An abstract, luminous portal or archway made of shifting, iridescent chrome, opening onto a soft, pastel dreamcore sky with gentle, drifting clouds.

caption:
Okay, so this hit me hard: what if your "personality" was mostly a brilliant, complex safe house your nervous system built? Time to feel that truth, no fixing.
